Distinct Until Changed Behavior

Distinct Until Changed is an operator behavior that prevents redundant pipeline execution by suppressing emissions when the resolved and merged pipeline value is considered equivalent to the previously emitted value under the configured comparison strategy.

Distinct Until Changed Contract Summary

  • Operates exclusively within the Operator stage
  • Evaluates the fully resolved and merged pipeline value
  • The first encountered value always proceeds through the pipeline
  • Subsequent equivalent values are suppressed
  • Suppression is expressed by returning VAULT_NOOP, which ends pipeline execution for the current run
  • Comparison is performed using either a user-supplied equality function or the default structural comparison
  • Does not mutate state and does not emit snapshots directly

Distinct Until Changed participates in value admission control. Its sole responsibility is to determine whether a newly produced pipeline value represents a meaningful change compared to the previously emitted value. When no meaningful change is detected, downstream pipeline stages are skipped and no snapshot is produced.

This behavior is commonly used to eliminate duplicate emissions caused by repeated inputs, identical resolution results, or idempotent update flows. By suppressing redundant pipeline executions early, it helps reduce unnecessary filtering, reduction, and rendering work without altering pipeline semantics.

Note

When no custom comparison function is supplied, the operator determines equality by performing a structural JSON comparison of the incoming value and the last emitted value. If the two values are structurally identical, the update is suppressed and no downstream pipeline stages execute. 

{{`JSON.stringify(incoming) === JSON.stringify(lastEmittedValue);`}}
Distinct Until Changed Behavior

Distinct Until Changed is an operator behavior that performs value-level deduplication within the Operator stage. It evaluates the resolved and merged pipeline value and suppresses further pipeline execution for the current pipeline run when that value is equivalent to the previously emitted value.

This behavior always allows the first encountered value to proceed through the pipeline. For subsequent pipeline executions, the incoming value is compared against the last successfully emitted value. If the values are considered equivalent, the operator suppresses the update by returning VAULT_NOOP.

When suppression occurs, the current pipeline execution ends for that run. Downstream stages—including filters, reducers, and taps—are skipped, and no snapshot is emitted. The pipeline remains available to process future candidates, which may be emitted if they differ from the last accepted value.

Equality determination may be performed using either a user-supplied comparison function or the default structural comparison strategy. This allows distinctness to be defined according to domain-specific semantics without altering pipeline structure or reducer logic.

Distinct Until Changed does not mutate state, does not emit snapshots directly, and does not influence pipeline scheduling or lifecycle control. Its responsibility is strictly limited to deciding whether a pipeline candidate represents a meaningful change relative to the previous emission.

Behavior Scope

This operator is applied explicitly via the fluent .operators() API during FeatureCell initialization. When registered, it participates in the Operator stage alongside any other configured operators and is evaluated in the order declared.

Distinct Until Changed is most effective when used as an early admission control mechanism to eliminate redundant pipeline executions caused by repeated inputs, idempotent resolutions, or unchanged upstream values.

Operator Stage Diagram
Distinct Until Changed Behavior
DistinctComparison<T>
Property Description

compare

inputs:

  • a: T
  • b: T

type:

  • (a: T, b: T) => boolean

return:

  • boolean

optional

Optional comparison function used by the Distinct Until Changed operator to determine whether the incoming pipeline value should be considered equivalent to the previously emitted pipeline value.

When provided, this function is invoked with the new incoming value and the last successfully emitted value. If the function returns true, the values are treated as equal and the update is suppressed.

If no comparison function is supplied, the operator falls back to the default structural comparison strategy.

The comparison function must be pure, deterministic, and free of side effects. It must not mutate either argument and must return a consistent result for the same input values across executions.

Evaluation Outcomes

Distinct Until Changed determines whether an incoming pipeline value should be emitted or suppressed by comparing it against the last successfully emitted value. This comparison is performed for each pipeline execution after resolve and merge.

By default, the operator uses a structural comparison strategy to determine equality. When a custom comparison function is supplied, that function becomes the authoritative definition of what it means for two values to be considered equivalent.

In all cases, the first encountered value is always emitted. Subsequent values are evaluated relative to the most recent emitted value. If a value is considered equal under the active comparison strategy, the operator returns VAULT_NOOP, ending the current pipeline execution for that run.

Example 1: Default Comparison (Primitive Values)
Incoming Value Result
5

(first emission)

 Value is emitted (first value always passes through)
5

(same as previous)

 VAULT_NOOP — value is considered equal to the previously emitted value and is suppressed
9 Value is emitted (value differs from previous emission)
Example 2: Default Comparison (Structured Values)
Incoming Value Result
{ id: 1, name: "A" }

(first emission)

 Value is emitted
{ id: 1, name: "A" }

(structurally equivalent)

 VAULT_NOOP — structurally equivalent to the previously emitted value
{ id: 2, name: "A" } Value is emitted (value differs from previous emission)
Example 3: Custom Comparison (Identifier-Based Equality)

When a custom comparison function is provided, it replaces the default structural comparison entirely. The function is invoked with the incoming value and the last successfully emitted value and must explicitly determine whether the two values should be treated as equivalent.

In this example, the comparison function evaluates only a stable identifier (id) and ignores all other properties. As a result, values with the same identifier are considered equal even if other fields differ.

Incoming Value Result
{ id: 1, name: "B" }

(id unchanged)

 VAULT_NOOP — custom comparison considers values equivalent
{ id: 1, name: "X" }

(id unchanged)

 VAULT_NOOP — custom comparison considers values equivalent
{ id: 2, name: "X" } Value is emitted (custom comparison detects a change)
Actual Comparison Function for Example 3
{{`// Custom comparison function
const compareById = (a: { id: number }, b: { id: number }) => {
  return a.id === b.id;
};

// Registering the operator with a custom comparison function
this.vault
  .operators(
    [
      withDistinctUntilChanged(compareById)
    ]
  )
  .initialize();`}}
 
{{`// Custom comparison function
const compareById = (a: { id: number }, b: { id: number }) => {

};

// Registering the operator with a custom comparison function
employeeCell

Examples

Distinct Until Changed is enabled by attaching the withDistinctUntilChanged operator behavior via the fluent API during FeatureCell initialization. When no comparison function is supplied, the operator uses the default structural comparison to suppress duplicate values.

Example 1: Configure a FeatureCell with Distinct Until Changed

In this example, the operator suppresses consecutive equivalent pipeline values that are structurally equivalent to the previously emitted value. The first value always passes through; subsequent equivalent values are suppressed and do not reach downstream stages. 

{{`@FeatureCell`}}<Employee[][]>{{`('employees')
@Injectable({
  providedIn: 'root'
})
export class EmployeeService {
  private readonly vault = injectVault`}}<Employee[][]>{{`(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    // Apply one or more operators during initialization
    this.vault
      .operators(
        [
          withDistinctUntilChanged()
        ]
      )
      .initialize();
  }
}`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell`}}<Employee[]>{{`(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: [],
  },
  [
    // Operator behaviors are not registered as part of the
    // FeatureCell's declarative configuration.
  ]
);

// Apply distinct-until-changed during initialization
employeeCell
  .operators(
    [
      withDistinctUntilChanged()
    ]
  )
  .initialize();`}}
